subject: Whistic onboarding: scope reconciliation & evidence claims request
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightleaf.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightleaf.com, sec-devops@brightleaf.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Whistic onboarding: scope reconciliation & evidence claims request

Hi Mateo / Camila —

Thanks for agreeing to start the vendor security intake for Brightleaf procurement. We're kicking off a short Whistic/SIG/CAIQ review to validate scope and collected evidence before our SSO & procurement approval. Action items and asks below — hoping to close the first pass in 10 business days.

High-level asks:
- Confirm which Whistic profile fields we should populate (CAIQ subset vs. full SIG).
- For each SIG/CAIQ claim, assign an owner and point to existing evidence (S3 presigned URL, public docs, SOC2 report).
- Provide a small sample of the latest SOC 2 (summary + auditor name) and any KMS/TLS attestations.
- Confirm data residency and whether we use gov/regional endpoints (they flagged EU data residency as a potential requirement).

Attachments: Brightleaf_SIG_template_v2.xlsx (SIG mapping template).

Timeline: can you confirm owners and any existing evidence links by EOD 2026-12-08? If not feasible, propose a short window.

If it helps, procurement needs the CAIQ claim mapping and an evidence inhalation plan (who will upload to Whistic and when).

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Anita Shah
Security Program Manager
Brightleaf
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightleaf.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Whistic onboarding: scope reconciliation & evidence claims request

Anita — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the 2026-12-08 target for initial owners and links. Quick answers up-front:

Scope recommendation:
- We typically surface the CAIQ core + SIG-lite fields for procurement (fewer free-text items). If Brightleaf needs a full SIG, note that will require a faster evidence upload cadence.

Initial owners (proposed):
- SSO & auth evidence: Camila Reyes (camila_reyes@redwood.com)
- KMS / crypto / TLS artifacts: Mina Haddad (mina_haddad@redwood.com)
- Evidence uploads, Whistic account admin & manifest: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com)

Evidence we can provide now:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary + auditor contact) — attached.
- S3 presigned samples for log retention and SOC artifacts (we can create short-lived presigned links for bulk upload).
- KMS rotation proof and TLS cert chain (Mina will attach).

Questions:
- Can you confirm if Brightleaf requires EU-only hosting for any service we provide, or is an EU data residency flag sufficient for now?
- Will procurement need a signed attestation (DocuSign) or is portal proof possession enough?

We will:
1) Map SIG/CAIQ claims to internal evidence names and owners by 2026-12-08.
2) Prep a single manifest CSV for Ben to upload to Whistic once access is granted.

Thanks — I'll follow up internally with a task matrix and owners.

— Mateo Alvarez
Vendor Security Lead, Redwood Inference
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Brightleaf Whistic intake — owners & tasks (please ack)

Team — looping you in from Anita at Brightleaf. High-level plan and rough owners (please ack or reassign):

Tasks / owner / ETA:
- Review Brightleaf_SIG_template_v2.xlsx and mark which claims we can auto-populate (Camila) — due 2026-12-06.
- Gather SOC2 artifacts and a one-page summary (Mateo + Mina) — due 2026-12-04.
- Produce presigned upload URLs and sample manifest for Whistic ingest (Ben) — due 2026-12-07.
- Confirm KMS/TLS proofs and provide cert chain (Mina) — due 2026-12-04.
- Flag any claims that require legal attestation (I will loop legal if needed).

Notes / approach:
- We'll map SIG control IDs to our internal doc names in the task-matrix.csv (attached). The procurement team prefers a single CSV with claim, owner, evidence link, and evidence type.
- If Brightleaf requests full SIG, call out the live evidence windows (Whistic tends to expire presigned URLs quickly).
- Use drive:redwood/whistic/brightleaf-kickoff for drafts. I'll add a short walkthrough doc for Ben on the Whistic upload expectations.

Attachments: task-matrix.csv

Please reply with ACK and any reassignments.

— Mateo
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightleaf.com>
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, procurement@brightleaf.com
Date: 2026-12-02T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Whistic onboarding: scope reconciliation & evidence claims request

Anita — thanks. Mateo sent the task matrix to our drive and we're standing up the upload plan. Quick operational notes: 
- We will provision a Whistic contributor account for our uploads; please share the admin invite or invite ben_carter@redwood.com.
- For presigned S3 links: we'll provide a timeboxed bundle (48h window) for bulk ingest.
- If you prefer incremental uploads, we can do a weekly cadence for any remaining claims.

Quoted for context:
> "Timeline: can you confirm owners and any existing evidence links by EOD 2026-12-08?"

We will meet the 12-08 target for initial claim-owner mapping. After that, I'll open the upload window — proposing 2026-12-09 -> 2026-12-11 for the bulk presign window.

— Ben Carter
Security Integrations Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@brightleaf.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, procurement@brightleaf.com
Date: 2026-12-03T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Whistic onboarding: scope reconciliation & evidence claims request

Ben / team — perfect, that window works. We'll provision the Whistic contributor invite to ben_carter@redwood.com and procurement will confirm DocuSign requirements if any. One small ask — please add a short readme file in the manifest that explains which claims are "attestation" vs "proof of possession". That helps our reviewers triage faster.

Looking forward to the manifest and presigned links.

— Anita
Security Program Manager, Brightleaf
